LESSON: THE CONSTITUTION OF KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Development and Governance
Topic 5.2: The Constitution of Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The Constitution of Kenya, part of Political Development and Governance in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should a country have a constitution? 2. Why should we uphold and protect the Constitution?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. discuss the importance of the Constitution of Kenya for social wellbeing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. analyse ways of upholding and protecting the Constitution of Kenya for social cohesion,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply the national values in day-to-day life as provided in the Constitution of Kenya for promotion of good governance,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of The Constitution of Kenya in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. uphold and protect the Constitution of Kenya for promotion of ethical and responsible citizenship. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Constitution of Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
